concepts.hook: *Skelra*, the oar that snapped in a storm off the Leeward shoals and was rowed home on one blade, so its stroke still goes on.
*Lesk*, the iron that opens wet knots, set in the sky by a rope-mender who could not open the knot that held her son's boat.
*Hatun*, the scoop a mother used to bail a sinking boat to the last, and the sky keeps it bailing the dark.
*Oskel*, the lead on a knotted line that voyagers drop to find bottom, and which has never yet touched the bottom of Vel.
*Sket*, the bone hook used to haul a drowned body over the gunwale, which the sky holds out to those still in the water.
*Tharn*, the gutting knife left on a stone at the tide line by a man who walked out toward the Unflown and never came back.
*Tirun*, a boat that came home keel-up with no crew aboard and its lamps still lit underneath.
*Mesul*, a ferry that carries the drowned across the Leeward sea, which the islanders say touches no shore on the far side.
*Ommen*, the boat that carries one lantern for every name said aloud at the harbour mouth on the night of the drowning.
*Ilthun*, a ketch that went through the storm of Tavo with its stern stove in and still sails with its sails full.
*Vesket*, the goods boat laden with salt for the islands, whose captain is still counting the bags in the dark.
*Hesta*, the old sailcloth stitched around a drowned body in the Leeward yards, flown above the bay for one year after the burial.
*Mekle*, the wool cap a fisher's widow knitted for her son and left on a rock, which hangs above the harbour mouth in the cold months.
*Hosk*, the coat that kept the sea out of its wearer until the wearer was carried out to sea inside it.
*Kunath*, a sleeve torn off on a gaff that still reaches out in the sky as if to take hold of another hand.
*Tessal*, the kettle a voyager sets on for the one who never comes home, said never to boil in the Leeward sky.
*Ulkun*, the pot every trader keeps for the crew's share, which the sky tips only at the new moon.
*Mirkan*, a bowl that split in the cold, mended with pitch and sent out to the Unflown for luck.
*Sorn*, the wooden lid that keeps a hearth's warmth in while the voyagers are away, and which no one has yet lifted.
*Thessa*, the shuttle whose sailcloth is always unfinished in the sky because the weaver's thread ran out in the middle of a row.
*Hanor*, the stone on a line that measures how far a mast fell when it went over, and which still swings in the Leeward dark.
*Lutha*, the small lamp set on a prow to show a boat the way in, of which the sky has many, and one still burning.
*Ketha*, the mending shuttle that Kael is said to borrow when he casts for fallen stars and never catches one.
*Tiskel*, the box kite flown over the water for a drowned child, which the family sends up again each spring.
*Sarra*, the kite that cuts the lines of other kites in a Leeward contest, and whose cut string drifted off into the Upper Sea.
*Kattal*, the sea-anchor kite that holds a drifting boat's nose into the wind until dawn.
*Tunnal*, a kite carrying a bell that rings a warning through fog for boats that cannot see the shore.
*Hulket*, the kite flown by the foolish youth of a crew to dance over the storm, at which Tavo laughs and does not tear it.
*Nelu*, a kite flown from one boat to another across rough water, carrying a salt token that proves the bargain.
*Sathrun*, the long-tailed kite a wife flies each dusk for a ferry that is not yet home.
